title: WMAP nine-year: a six-parameter Lambda-CDM fit, with limits that are model constraints
summary: Hinshaw and colleagues say the nine-year WMAP data are fit by six-parameter Lambda-CDM, and they quote limits such as r < 0.13 that are limits inside that model class.
body: The abstract of Hinshaw and colleagues says the final nine-year WMAP data, alone and with other data, continue to be fit by a six-parameter Lambda-CDM model. When WMAP is combined with high-l CMB anisotropy, the BAO scale, and the Hubble constant, it says Omega_b h^2, Omega_c h^2, and Omega_Lambda are each determined to about 1.5 percent. It reports evidence for a tilt in the primordial spectrum at the 5-sigma level. Examples of limits on departures from the six-parameter model: tensor-to-scalar ratio r < 0.13 at 95 percent confidence; spatial curvature −0.0027 (+0.0039/−0.0038); summed neutrino mass < 0.44 eV at 95 percent confidence; relativistic species 3.84 ± 0.40 when the full data are analyzed. These are parameter constraints of a fitted model. The abstract presents them as such. A limit such as r < 0.13 is not a detection of gravitational waves.
